literal: Ruin and prosperity are not non-existent; unswervingness of the mind is the ornament to the noble.
translation: Loss and gain are inevitable in life; maintaining an unswerving, impartial mind through both is the true ornament of the noble.
modern: கேடும் பெருக்கமும் வாழ்வில் இல்லாதவை அல்ல; நெஞ்சத்தில் கோணாமல் நடுவுநிலையோடு இருப்பதே சான்றோர்க்கு அழகாகும்.
explanation: This couplet explains that adversity and prosperity are natural, inevitable phases of human life. Since these fluctuations are bound to happen, the truly noble person does not let their mind bend or deviate from fairness because of them. Keeping the mind upright and impartial in both good times and bad is the finest ornament a virtuous person can wear. The word 'kōṭāmai' (not bending) beautifully captures the essence of neutrality and justice under all circumstances.
